# sta310r

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/eribul/sta310r/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/eribul/sta310r/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Package documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-eribul.github.io%2Fsta310r-blue)](https://eribul.github.io/sta310r/)
<!-- badges: end -->

`sta310r` collects the data sets that accompany Collett (2023), *Modelling
Survival Data in Medical Research* (4th edition), together with a small set of
teaching functions that implement the estimators used in the STA310 course at
the University of Gothenburg from first principles. The estimators are written
so that the individual steps can be inspected in the computer
exercises, and they agree with the established implementations in [survival](https://github.com/therneau/survival) to within numerical tolerance.

## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pak::pak("eribul/sta310r")
```

## Name conflicts

The package includes six data sets with names also used by the `survival` package, for data
sets that are not the same:

- `bladder`
- `cgd`
- `kidney`
- `myeloma`
- `ovarian`
- `rats` 

Attach `sta310r` last (`library(sta310r)` AFTER `library(survival)`), or use `sta310r::xxx` explicitly if both packages are attached. You may also just refer to the datasets by their aliases as described below.

## Data sets by example

Each data set that is used in a worked example of Collett (2023) has an alias
`dX.Y`, where `X.Y` is the number of the example. For example, `d3.7` is the
`myeloma` data used in Example 3.7, and `d8.4` is the baseline cirrhosis data.
The aliases are ordinary data objects: `d3.7` works after `library(sta310r)`, and
`?d3.7` opens the help page of the data set. See
`vignette("datasets-by-exercise")`.

Note that 2 data sets are used in example 8.4 (hence no aliases used there). 

```{r}
library(sta310r)
dataset_by_exercise |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(chapter)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(chapter = paste(chapter, chapter_title, sep = ". ")) |>
  dplyr::select(chapter, example, alias, dataset, n_rows, n_variables) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "chapter", id = "datasets-by-example")
```

## Teaching functions

* `km_estimate()` and `plot_km()`: the Kaplan-Meier estimator with Greenwood
  standard errors, and a plot of it.
* `cox_fit()`: Cox regression fitted by Newton-Raphson, with Breslow or Efron
  handling of ties.
* `emp_hazard()`: empirical, piecewise constant hazard estimates.
* `n_events_logrank()`, `power_logrank()` and `power_logrank_sim()`: sample
  size, power and simulation for the log-rank test.
* `cif_cause_specific()`: cumulative incidence functions from cause-specific
  Cox models.

## Example

`km_estimate()` returns the risk sets, the events and censorings, the survivor
function and its standard error at each event time:

```{r}
km_estimate(iud$time, iud$status)
```

`cox_fit()` reproduces `survival::coxph()` on the same data:

```{r}
fit <- cox_fit(myeloma$time, myeloma$status, myeloma[, c("age", "bun")])
ref <- survival::coxph(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ age + bun, data = myeloma)
cbind(cox_fit = coef(fit), coxph = coef(ref))
```
